summary: Randomized prefetch splay during canary causes pinned-version ghosting and degraded fallbacks
description: Issue summary: During a staged canary deployment (15% weight) for redwood/gpt-open-13b-quant-v2 for Acme Analytics, a subset of tenant sessions that were explicitly pinned to the new variant observed silent fallbacks to the legacy compatibility variant. The behavior coincided with a burst of multipart chunked uploads and automated multipart retry traffic from the customer's ingestion pipeline. Impact: ~4% of requests from pinned sessions returned degraded variant responses and triggered an unexpected billing spike for the customer because some requests were rerouted to an on-demand fallback variant with higher token-cost settings. No user data was exposed; quality/consistency and cost were impacted. Environment: Production, us-east-1. Canary weight: 15%. Prewarm policy: probabilistic prefetch with randomized splay (0-30s). Observed around 2026-03-08T10:15-10:45 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create tenant with explicit model pin to redwood/gpt-open-13b-quant-v2
2) Start a steady stream of chunked/multipart requests that include a small metadata header mutation on retries (Content-Type: multipart/form-data -> application/octet-stream on retry),
3) Trigger canary rollout with 15% weight and probabilistic prewarm splay enabled for the target variant,

4) Observe routing logs and responses for pinned sessions over a 30-minute window; intermittent requests may be routed to legacy variant or degraded fallback after prewarm tombstone expiry or prewarm swap,
5) Reproduce more reliably by increasing post-deploy prewarm splay to 0-60s and sending high retry rate with header normalization changes.

investigation_notes: Initial findings: The routing decision chain checks pin affinity -> prewarm state -> header-stability rules -> fallback policy. Hypothesis: randomized prewarm splay caused prewarm instance lifecycle overlap and tombstone expiry, and multipart retry mutated Content-Type causing the header-stability guard to mark the request as incompatible with the primed KV-cache; orchestrator snapshot lag meant some edge routers still referenced the older snapshot that hadn't acknowledged the pin commit. Combined, these conditions triggered fallback routing even though the tenant was pinned. Evidence: repeated traces show identical session tokens where earlier requests used 'new' variant and later request (retry) went to legacy variant with identical shard assignment. We reproduced locally by forcing a 150ms snapshot commit delay and injecting header normalization on retry. Related to earlier tickets where prewarm tombstones suppressed pin commits under a race (see linked SUP-3141592).
hypothesis: Race between prewarm splay/tombstone TTL and orchestrator snapshot commit, exacerbated by header mutation on multipart retry, leads to contradictory routing decisions: edge deems request incompatible with primed variant and orchestrator snapshot lag prevents pin resolution, causing fallback to legacy variant.
mitigation_steps_taken: 1) Support: temporarily paused probabilistic prewarm splay for Acme Analytics' tenant to force deterministic prewarm (immediately lowered routing anomalies),
2) SRE: increased prewarm tombstone TTL from 25s -> 90s for affected canary cohort in us-east-1 while we investigate snapshot commit latency,
3) Billing: created a customer invoice credit for the observed 3-hour cost delta and initiated investigation to confirm exact token overage (finance ticket created).
4) Product: flagged model for non-automated rollout (manual promote) until guard changes deploy.
root_cause: Multiple interacting conditions: (a) probabilistic prewarm splay causing prewarm lifecycle overlap and earlier tombstone expiry; (b) orchestrator snapshot commit latency creating temporal mismatch in pin commitment across edge routers; (c) header-normalization behavior on multipart retries triggering header-stability fallback rule. The combined effect produced incorrect fallback routing for some pinned sessions.
resolution_plan: Short-term fixes (next 48 hours): 1) Disable probabilistic prewarm splay for canaries <20% for high-tier customers; 2) Increase prewarm tombstone TTL globally from 25s to 90s pending deeper perf analysis; 3) Add a routing guard to prefer pin-commit resolution when session token + tenant pin exist even if header changes are minor (Content-Type only), and add logging to capture header mutations that flip fallback decisions. Medium-term (2-4 weeks): 4) Improve orchestrator snapshot commit visibility and reduce commit tail latency; 5) Add end-to-end test harness that simulates multipart retries with header mutations across staged canary and prewarm windows; 6) Harden prewarm lifecycle state machine to avoid tombstone-induced pin suppression. Long-term: incorporate deterministic prewarm options in rollout UI and automatic rollback heuristics tied to pin-consistency telemetry.
resolution_status: In rollout - short-term mitigations applied; medium-term work scoped and assigned to orchestration and routing teams.
